title: Reconstructing Escalation Protocol Compliance Across Repeated Incidents
scenario_text:
**Zendesk — Organization: Lumen Dynamics (3 tickets, last 90 days)**

Ticket #ZD-46810 (Apr 5, 2026): Priority: High. Subject: 'SSO login failures intermittent.' Assigned: Tier 1 → Tier 2 (Apr 5). Resolved: Apr 7. Resolution: 'Auth service restart resolved. Monitoring.'
Internal note (Apr 7, @tier2-agent): 'Third SSO-related ticket in 6 months. Should this trigger escalation protocol per repeat-incident policy?'
[No response to internal note]

Ticket #ZD-47544 (May 12, 2026): Priority: Urgent. Subject: 'SSO completely broken — all users locked out.' Assigned: Tier 1 → Tier 2 (May 12) → Engineering (May 12). Resolved: May 13. CSAT: 1/5.
Customer comment (May 12): 'This is unacceptable. Same issue as last month. We need an RCA and a permanent fix commitment.'
Internal note (May 14, @alex.foster): 'Customer success is aware. Scheduling exec touchpoint.'

Ticket #ZD-49388 (Jun 24, 2026): Priority: Urgent. Subject: 'SSO failures AGAIN.' Status: Open. Opened 52 hours ago.
Customer comment (Jun 24): 'Third time. We are done. Legal is drafting a termination notice citing material breach of the uptime SLA. Your CEO will hear from ours.'

**Confluence — Repeat Incident Escalation Policy (v2, effective Feb 2026)**
Section 1: 'When a customer experiences 3+ incidents of the same root cause category within a rolling 6-month window, the following protocol is mandatory: (a) Automatic escalation to Support Escalation Manager; (b) RCA delivered within 5 business days; (c) Engineering assigns a DRI for permanent fix; (d) CSM schedules exec alignment within 10 business days.'
Section 3: 'Failure to trigger this protocol after the qualifying incident constitutes a process violation reportable to VP Support.'

**Jira — AUTH-2847 (created May 13, 2026)**
Type: Bug | Priority: High | Status: Backlog
Summary: 'Investigate recurring SSO failures for specific SAML configurations'
Assignee: Unassigned
Sprint: None
Comment (May 15, @eng-lead): 'Need to prioritize this. Adding to Sprint 26.4 candidates.'
Comment (Jun 2, @eng-lead): 'Pulled from 26.4 due to capacity. Targeting 26.5.'
:+1: reacted by @jordan.kim

**Slack — #cs-internal (May 14, 2026, 3:12 PM)**
@alex.foster: Heads up — Lumen Dynamics had another SSO failure. Second P1-equivalent in 6 weeks. One more and we hit the repeat-incident threshold.
@carlos.reyes: :eyes: Got it. If it happens again ping me immediately so we can trigger the protocol proactively.
@alex.foster: :thumbsup:

**Slack — #cs-internal (Jun 24, 2026, 10:15 AM)**
@alex.foster: @carlos.reyes Lumen SSO is down again. This is #3.
[No reply from carlos.reyes — OOO per Google Calendar Jun 23-25]

**Google Calendar — Carlos Reyes**
Jun 23-25, 2026: 'PTO — Beach Trip' (All day, OOO auto-reply enabled)
question: As of June 26 (Carlos returns from PTO), which required steps of the Repeat Incident Escalation Protocol have been completed for Lumen Dynamics, and what is the compliance status?

contributor.name: Carlos Reyes
contributor.title: Support Escalation Manager
contributor.domain_expertise: Severity triage, SLA management, cross-team coordination during incidents

choices: Protocol was triggered correctly on Jun 24 when Alex pinged Carlos in Slack. Carlos's OOO status constitutes force majeure; the 5-business-day RCA clock starts Jun 26 when he returns.
Protocol should not have triggered yet. The Apr 5 ticket was Priority: High, not P1, so it does not count toward the 3-incident threshold. Only two qualifying incidents exist (May 12 and Jun 24).
Protocol was never formally triggered. Zero of four required steps completed. Full process violation — reportable to VP Support per Section 3.

Protocol was partially triggered: CSM is aware (step d initiated informally via Slack), and Engineering has a Jira ticket (step c). Steps (a) and (b) were not completed. Partial compliance — needs remediation but not a formal violation.
